description: The baseline we monitor for every client, one section per item: infrastructure (node health, OOM kills, volume utilisation and saturation, HTTP 5xx/4xx/RPS), database load and disk, application HTTP requests, reliability (backup success and tooling errors), security (certificate expiry) and cost. Prometheus only - no Loki or Tempo dependency, so it renders on every cluster. Sections whose exporter is absent will be empty; each says which exporter it needs.

panels.title: Nodes Not Ready
panels.description: Nodes whose Ready condition is not true. Anything above zero is an incident.

panels.title: OOM Kills (24h)
panels.description: Containers killed for exceeding their memory limit in the last 24 hours, counted from cAdvisor's `container_oom_events_total` counter.

panels.title: Volumes >85% Full
panels.description: PersistentVolumeClaims past 85% utilisation. These fill up silently and take an application down with them.

panels.title: HTTP 5xx Rate
panels.description: Share of ingress requests answered 5xx.

panels.title: Backups Failing
panels.description: Velero schedules whose most recent backup did not succeed.

panels.title: Certs Expiring <30d
panels.description: Certificates within 30 days of expiry, from x509-certificate-exporter.

panels.title: Pods Not Running
panels.description: Pods stuck Failed or Pending.

panels.title: Spend (month to date)
panels.description: Cloud spend so far this month. Needs azure-cost-exporter.

panels.title: Node Ready Status
panels.description: 1 = Ready, 0 = NotReady, per node. Plotted over time rather than as a count so a node that flapped and recovered is still visible after the fact.

panels.title: Node Conditions
panels.description: Nodes currently reporting a pressure or network condition. An empty table is the healthy state.

panels.title: Node CPU & Memory Utilisation
panels.description: Per-node CPU and memory utilisation. Both are 0-1 fractions of the same node, so they share one axis honestly - this is not a dual-axis chart.

panels.title: Container OOM Kill Events
panels.description: Each bar is an OOM kill, attributed to a pod, from cAdvisor's `container_oom_events_total` counter. OOM kills are the most common cause of unexplained restarts and nothing else on the cluster reports them.

panels.title: Containers in a Bad State Now
panels.description: Containers whose last termination was an OOM kill, and containers currently in CrashLoopBackOff. These are kube-state-metrics gauges describing the present state - the panel to their left counts events over time.

panels.title: Volume Utilisation %
panels.description: Current fill level of every PVC. Orange at 75%, red at 85% - matching the 'PersistentVolume Usage' alert.

panels.title: Volume Utilisation over time
panels.description: Fill level over time. The slope is what matters: a volume at 60% and climbing 5%/day needs action sooner than one that has sat at 80% for a month. A bargauge cannot show this.

panels.title: Node Disk Saturation (I/O time)
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the device spent servicing I/O. This is the actual saturation signal: at 1.0 the disk is busy 100% of the time and every further request queues. IOPS and throughput below tell you what is driving it.

panels.title: Node Disk IOPS
panels.description: Completed read and write operations per second, per device.

panels.title: Node Disk Throughput
panels.description: Bytes read and written per second, per device.

panels.title: Request Rate by Status Class
panels.description: Total request volume, split by outcome.

panels.title: 5xx Error Rate & 4xx Rate
panels.description: Error rates as a share of all traffic. Both are fractions on one axis. 404 is excluded from the 4xx line because scanner noise otherwise buries real client errors.

panels.title: Request Volume vs 30m Baseline (anomaly)
panels.description: 5-minute request rate over the 30-minute rate. 1.0 is steady state. This is the RPS-anomaly signal - it flags a surge or a traffic collapse regardless of the cluster's absolute volume, which a raw RPS threshold cannot do.

panels.title: 4xx Spikes by Service
panels.description: Client errors per 5 minutes, attributed to a backend. Same expression as the '4XX spike' alert, so what you see here is what pages.

panels.title: DB CPU / Sessions / Storage %
panels.description: Azure SQL load and disk utilisation. All three are percentages of the same database, so one axis is correct.

panels.title: DB Connection Failures & Deadlocks
panels.description: Failed connections and deadlocks per 5 minutes.

options.content:
These panels read `azure_sql_database_*`, published by **azure-metrics-scraper**. On a cluster without it they will be empty — this row is collapsed by default for that reason, and it is the one section of this dashboard that is cloud-specific. For Postgres or MySQL, point the equivalent exporter at Prometheus and swap the metric names; the panel shapes (load %, disk %, connection failures) stay the same.

Deeper Azure SQL detail lives in the **Azure SQL — Health & Saturation** dashboard.

panels.title: Backup Status by Schedule
panels.description: Most recent outcome per Velero schedule, and how many hours ago the last success was. A schedule that reports success but whose last success is days old is still a failure - the status alone will not tell you.

panels.title: Backup Attempts vs Failures
panels.description: Backup runs over time, split by outcome. Partial failures are called out separately because they are silently useless: the backup exists but is incomplete.

panels.title: Errors on Deployed Tooling
panels.description: Infrastructure components we deploy that are not running: crash loops, image pull failures and config errors, scoped to the infra namespaces. Empty is the healthy state.

panels.title: Restarts of Deployed Tooling
panels.description: Restart events for the tooling we operate. A component restarting quietly on a schedule is the failure mode that never gets noticed.

panels.title: Days Until Certificate Expiry
panels.description: Remaining validity of every certificate x509-certificate-exporter can see. The lines slope down at one day per day; a renewal shows as a jump back up. A line that fails to jump before it reaches zero is a cert-manager renewal that did not happen.

panels.title: Certificates Expiring Soonest
panels.description: Every certificate ranked by how soon it expires. Orange under 30 days, red under 7.

targets.expr: sort(min by (secret_namespace, secret_name, subject_CN, issuer_CN) ((x509_cert_not_after - time()) / 86400))

panels.title: Daily Cloud Spend
panels.description: Spend per calendar day. The exporter puts the date in a `dateISO` label rather than on the time axis, so this is a bar chart over that label, not a time series. Needs azure-cost-exporter.

panels.title: Spend Rate vs 7-Day Average (spike detection)
panels.description:
Spend over the last 24h divided by the trailing 7-day daily average, both derived from the month-to-date total (a real time series, unlike the per-day label metric). 1.0 is normal; above ~1.25 something changed - a new node pool, a runaway job, an egress spike. An absolute spend threshold cannot tell growth from a spike, this ratio can.

Caveat: the month-to-date counter resets on the 1st, so this reads low for the first week of each month.

list.name: namespace
list.label: Namespace
list.description: Scopes the workload panels (OOM, volumes, restarts). Node, HTTP, backup, certificate and cost panels are cluster-wide and ignore it.

list.name: infraNamespace
list.label: Infra Namespaces
list.description: Namespaces holding tooling we deploy and are responsible for. Drives the 'Errors on Deployed Tooling' panels. Set a sensible default per cluster, e.g. monitoring, argocd, cert-manager, velero, traefik-system, external-secrets.
